messages.subject: Time-removal (multinomPois): prediction units?
parts:
Hello unmarked gurus,

I am running removal models using multinomPois based on 10-min point counts split into 5, 2-min intervals.

How does unmarked know that we want densities/ha as our output if we can't/don't specify in the time-removal model statement (like we do in the distsamp model statements)?  Is there a way to specify this using multinomPois?  

My current time-removal multinomPois model statement:
year.mins_cc.lform<-multinomPois(~year+mins~cc+lform,data=umf)

Distsamp model statement:
year.mins_cc.lform<-distsamp(~year+mins~cc+lform,keyfun="hazard", unitsOut="ha", output="density",data=umf)

Thanks so much!

Sarah

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Time-removal (multinomPois): prediction units?
parts: A Poisson regression models the expected count in a given sample, so if you want densities you just have to do the conversion based on the area of your sample (e.g., plot size).  If the plot size changes across sampling units you need to include the log of plot size as a covariate for abundance (or as an offset, if that's available in multinomPois).  Then your expected count is the number of individuals in a plot with a unit area of 1.
